issues.description: signing_mode_enum is a partial function: the (not is_hex and safe_mode) branch falls through to the bare return
issues.detail: The free function in wallet_request_types.py enumerates three of four boolean combinations with elif, then returns CHIP_0002 unconditionally. The control flow is unstructured: the postcondition 'returns the mode matching (is_hex, safe_mode)' is satisfied only by accident of the final case. State the truth table explicitly with a single match/dispatch so a reader need not simulate four if-branches mentally.

issues.description: verify_signature has dead control flow: is_valid True path is unreachable when address check passes-and-fails
issues.detail: After the address branch may return False, the function then tests is_valid. But if is_valid is False and address is None, we fall through to the else returning 'Signature is invalid.' Acceptable, yet the structure 'if address...return; if is_valid return else return' conflates two orthogonal postconditions. Separate 'signature cryptographically valid' from 'binding to address valid' as two named predicates; current nesting invites future bugs.

issues.description: sign_message dispatch lacks an explicit total specification over SigningMode
issues.detail: The else-branch silently treats every unenumerated SigningMode as CHIP_0002. verify_signature, by contrast, raises on unsupported modes. The two functions disagree on the precondition for 'mode'. Pick one discipline and enforce it: either both are total over the enum (exhaustive match) or both refuse the unknown. Asymmetric handling of the same enum is exactly the kind of folklore Dijkstra refuses.

issues.description: test_sign_message_by_address never asserts the verify result
issues.detail: The test awaits verify_signature and discards the return value. The postcondition under test is 'verify returns isValid=True'; the code asserts nothing of the kind. This is tested-not-proved in the most literal sense: the test passes if verify_signature returns any object, including VerifySignatureResponse(isValid=False). Add the assertion.

issues.description: Misleading identifier: variable named hex_message holds non-hex bytes in three of four branches
issues.detail: In sign_message the local is named hex_message but is assigned UTF-8 bytes, raw bytes.fromhex output, and a tree hash. The name is a lie in three branches out of four. Rename to message_bytes or signing_payload. Names that misrepresent their contents are exactly the smuggled noise that makes correctness arguments harder than they need to be.

issues.description: Stale docstring 'param request' carried into verify_signature with no request parameter
issues.detail: The function now takes keyword args (signing_mode, public_key, message, signature, address) but the docstring still reads ':param request:'. A trivial issue, but documentation that lies about the signature is worse than no documentation. Either describe the actual parameters or remove the stub.

review.summary: The extraction is the right structural move: ad-hoc copies of the same five-branch dispatch in Wallet, DIDWallet, and NFTWallet are replaced by a single signing utility. The discipline of the extraction is uneven, however. The new signing_mode_enum free function relies on a final fall-through rather than an exhaustive match; sign_message and verify_signature disagree on whether unknown modes are an error or silently default; one of the two new tests forgets to assert anything; and a local named hex_message holds non-hex bytes in three of four branches. The control flow is structured, but the specifications behind it are not stated, and that is where the next defect will arrive.
